paragraphs: Hertz Holdings was incorporated in Delaware in 2015 to serve as the top-level holding company for Rental Car Intermediate Holdings, LLC, which wholly owns Hertz, Hertz Global's primary operating company. Hertz was incorporated in Delaware in 1967 and is a successor to corporations that have been engaged in the vehicle rental and leasing business since 1918.

We are engaged principally in the business of renting vehicles primarily through our Hertz, Dollar and Thrifty brands. As of December 31, 2025, we operated our vehicle rental business globally from approximately 11,000 company-operated and franchisee locations across approximately 160 countries and jurisdictions, including the U.S., Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia, Canada, the Caribbean, Latin America, the Middle East and New Zealand. We are one of the largest worldwide vehicle rental companies and our Hertz brand name is among the most recognized globally. We have an extensive network of airport and off airport rental locations in the U.S. and major European markets. We also operate the Hertz Car Sales brand, which offers a range of quality, competitively-priced used cars for sale online and at locations across the U.S.

Through our "Back-to-Basics" roadmap, we are committed to executing a comprehensive strategy to transform our business, anchored by three financial pillars: disciplined fleet management, revenue optimization and rigorous cost control. Building on our brand strength, global network and fleet management expertise, we remain committed to operational excellence and keeping customers central to everything we do. We have strengthened our fleet by refining our capabilities by sourcing vehicles strategically, deploying them efficiently and monetizing them effectively. Our approach balances disciplined execution today with systematic innovation for tomorrow, leveraging industry experience to adapt to evolving market dynamics and position us for sustainable growth in the future of mobility.
The Company has identified two reportable segments, which are consistent with its operating segments, as follows:

•Americas RAC - Rental of vehicles, as well as sales of vehicles and value-added services, in the U.S., Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean. We maintain a substantial network of company-operated rental locations in this segment and we have franchisees and partners that operate rental locations under our brands; and

•International RAC - Rental of vehicles, as well as sales of vehicles and value-added services, in locations other than the U.S., Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean. We maintain a substantial network of company-operated rental locations, a majority of which are in Europe, and we have franchisees and partners that operate rental locations under our brands. As of December 31, 2025, over 70% of our franchised locations were in markets covered by our International RAC segment.
In addition to the two reportable segments, we have corporate operations. We assess performance and allocate resources based upon the financial information for our operating segments.

For further financial information on our segments, see (i) "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations–Results of Operations and Selected Operating Data by Segment" in Part II, Item 7 of this 2025 Annual Report and (ii) Note 19, "Segment Information," in Part II, Item 8 of this 2025 Annual Report.
HERTZ GLOBAL HOLDINGS, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES THE HERTZ CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES ITEM 1. BUSINESS (Continued)

Our Americas RAC and International RAC vehicle rental businesses are primarily operated through our three largest brands — Hertz, Dollar, and Thrifty. We offer multiple brands to provide customers a full range of rental services at different price points, levels of service, offerings and products. These brands generally maintain separate rental locations (e.g., separate airport counters), and use distinct reservation, marketing and other customer contact activities. We achieve synergies across our brands by, among other things, utilizing a single fleet and fleet management team and, where applicable, combined vehicle maintenance, vehicle cleaning and back office functions.

Our top tier brand, Hertz, is one of the most recognized brands in the world. It offers premium customer service, as evidenced by the numerous published best-in-class vehicle rental awards that the brand has been awarded over time, both in the U.S. and internationally. The Hertz brand's tagline of "Hertz. Let's Go!" expresses our commitment to quality, seamless travel. The Hertz brand provides customers with several innovative offerings, primarily through its loyalty program Hertz Gold+, as well as access to vehicles offered through our specialty collections. The Hertz brand seeks to maintain its position as a premier provider of vehicle rental services through an intense focus on service, loyalty, quality and product innovation.

Our smart value brand, Dollar, is marketed as a smart choice for financially focused travelers looking for a dependable car. The Dollar brand's core focus is serving family, leisure and small business travelers through the airport vehicle rental channel, both in the U.S. and internationally. Dollar's tagline of "We never forget whose dollar it is" expresses the brand's mission of providing a reliable rental experience at a price that works.

Our deep value brand, Thrifty, competes as a cost-conscious offering for travelers seeking to find a good deal. The Thrifty brand's core focus is serving leisure travelers through the airport vehicle rental channel, both in the U.S. and internationally. Thrifty's tagline of "The Absolute Best Car for Your Money" expresses the brand's focus on being the rental brand that puts the customer in control of where to splurge and where to save.

We operate our brands at both airport and off airport locations that utilize common vehicle fleets, are supervised by common country, regional and local area management, use many common systems and rely on common vehicle maintenance and administrative centers. Additionally, our airport and off airport locations utilize common marketing activities and have many of the same customers. We regard both types of locations as aspects of a single, unitary vehicle rental business. Off airport revenues comprised 34% of our worldwide vehicle rental revenues in 2025 and 2024. Our Americas RAC vehicle rental operations have company-operated locations in the U.S. and Canada. Our International RAC vehicle rental operations have company-operated locations primarily in Australia, Belgium, the Czech Republic, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Slovakia, Spain and the U.K.

headings: The mix of program and non-program vehicles in our fleet, as well as declining values of our non-program vehicles, can subject us to an increased residual value risk.
We may not be able to effectively dispose of non-program vehicles, at the times or through the channels, that we desire.
Our vehicle carrying costs, customer service scores and ability to dispose of vehicles at acceptable prices and times may be negatively impacted if we lengthen the age of our fleet.
The failure of a manufacturer of our program vehicles to fulfill its obligations under a repurchase or guaranteed depreciation program could expose us to losses on those program vehicles.
Manufacturer safety recalls could require costly and time-consuming repairs to our fleet.
Our vehicle rental business is particularly sensitive to reductions in the levels of business and leisure travel.

Our business is highly seasonal, and any occurrence that disrupts rental activity during our peak periods could materially adversely affect our results of operations, financial condition, liquidity and cash flows.
We may be unable to accurately estimate future levels of rental activity and adjust the number, location and mix of vehicles used in our rental operations accordingly.
Our EV fleet exposes us to a number of risks.
We may fail to adequately respond to changes in technology that are impacting the mobility industry.
We face intense competition that may lead to downward pricing or an inability to increase prices.
If our customers develop loyalty to internet travel intermediaries rather than our brands, our business and revenues could be adversely affected.
Our commercial off airport leases and airport concession agreements expose us to numerous risks that could cause our financial results to suffer.
Maintaining favorable brand recognition is essential to our success and failure to do so could materially adversely affect our business.
The ability to attract and retain front-line employees, senior leadership and other key personnel is critical to the success of our business.
We may face issues with our union-represented employees.
If we fail to evaluate, maintain, upgrade and consolidate our information technology systems, our business could be adversely affected.

We may face particular data protection and privacy risks in connection with the European Union's Global Data Protection Regulation, the California Consumer Privacy Act and other privacy laws and regulations.
Our U.S. and foreign operations expose us to risks that may materially adversely affect our results of operations, financial condition, liquidity and cash flows.
The disposition of revenue earning vehicles may result in taxable income, which might not be fully offset by the taxable expense associated with newly purchased revenue earning vehicles.
Our ability to utilize our net operating loss carryforwards ("NOLs") may be limited as a result of ownership change under Section 382 of the Code.
We face risks related to liabilities and insurance.
paragraphs: Our business is subject to significant risks and uncertainties, and they should be carefully considered along with all of the information in this 2025 Annual Report. We believe that the information in this Item 1A., "Risk Factors" identifies the material risks and uncertainties most likely to affect Hertz Global and Hertz; however, these are not the only risks and uncertainties that we encounter in our operations. Additional risks and uncertainties that are not currently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial may also materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition, liquidity and cash flows in future periods. In such a case, you may lose all or part of your investment in Hertz Global's common stock or The Hertz Corporation's debt securities. You should carefully consider each of the following risks and uncertainties. Any of the following risks and uncertainties could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition, liquidity and cash flows in future periods.

We use program and non-program vehicles in our fleet. With program vehicles, vehicle manufacturers agree to repurchase the vehicles at a specified price or guarantee the depreciation rate on the vehicles during a specified time period. Using program vehicles in our fleet reduces our residual value risk and effectively provides fixed depreciation on those vehicles. Additionally, program vehicles provide flexibility because we may be able to sell certain program vehicles at a higher value during certain time periods than what we could for a similar non-program vehicle, enabling us to better manage our vehicle supply for our peak rental demand periods. These benefits diminish when there are fewer program vehicles in our fleet, which had generally been the case in recent years, but is improving. There can be no guarantee that we will be able to obtain the right mix of program and non-program vehicles in our fleet.

The significant majority of vehicles in our fleet are non-program vehicles. Overall, the percentage of our non-program fleet that we hold exposes us to residual value risk. Decreases in residual values of our non-program vehicles, or the failure of residual values to follow historical patterns, could result in a substantial loss on the sale of such vehicles, or accelerated depreciation while we own the vehicles. Each of these outcomes can materially adversely affect our results of operations, financial condition, liquidity and cash flows.

Vehicle residual values are variable and subject to market conditions, as well as seasonal fluctuations. If vehicle residual values decline, we may experience a greater risk of loss on vehicle sales, an increase in depreciation expense, a negative impact on our results of operations, and we may also experience challenges in meeting collateral requirements in our fleet financing facilities.

If there is a decline in residual values for non-program vehicles in our fleet and those residual values fail to improve, it may cause us to hold vehicles longer, sustain a substantial loss on the sale for such vehicles or require us to depreciate those vehicles at a more accelerated rate than previously anticipated while we own them.

If the market value of the vehicles in our fleet is reduced or our ability to sell vehicles in the used vehicle marketplace were to become severely limited, we may have difficulty meeting collateral requirements under our asset-backed financing arrangements, requiring us to either reduce the outstanding principal amount of debt or provide more collateral (in the form of cash, vehicles and/or certain other contractual rights) to the creditors under any such affected arrangement.

paragraphs: Hertz Global Holdings, Inc. is a holding company and its principal, wholly owned subsidiary is The Hertz Corporation. Hertz Global consolidates Hertz for financial statement purposes, and Hertz comprises approximately the entire balance of Hertz Global's assets, liabilities and operating cash flows. In addition, Hertz's operating revenues and operating expenses comprise nearly 100% of Hertz Global's revenues and operating expenses. As such, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") that follows herein is for Hertz and also applies to Hertz Global in all material respects, unless otherwise noted. Differences between the operations and results of Hertz and Hertz Global are separately disclosed and explained.

Our actual results may differ materially from those contained in or implied by any forward-looking statements. You should read the following MD&A together with the sections entitled "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements and Summary of Risk Factors," Item 1A, "Risk Factors" and our consolidated financial statements and related notes included in Part II, Item 8 of this 2025 Annual Report.
In this MD&A, we refer to the following non-GAAP measure and key metrics:

•Adjusted Corporate EBITDA – important non-GAAP measure to management because it allows management to assess the operational performance of our business, exclusive of certain items, and allows management to assess the performance of the entire business on the same basis as the segment measure of profitability. Management believes that it is important to investors for the same reasons it is important to management and because it allows investors to assess our operational performance on the same basis that management uses internally. Adjusted EBITDA, the segment measure of profitability and accordingly a GAAP measure, is calculated exclusive of certain items which are largely consistent with those used in the calculation of Adjusted Corporate EBITDA.

•Vehicle Utilization – important key metric to management and investors as it is the measurement of the proportion of our vehicles that are being used to generate revenues relative to rentable fleet capacity. Higher Vehicle Utilization means more vehicles are being utilized to generate revenues.

•Depreciation Per Unit Per Month – important key metric to management and investors as depreciation of revenue earning vehicles and lease charges is one of our largest expenses for the vehicle rental business and is driven by the number of vehicles, expected residual values at the expected time of disposal and expected hold period of the vehicles. Depreciation Per Unit Per Month is reflective of how we are managing the costs of our vehicles and facilitates a comparison with other participants in the vehicle rental industry.

•Total Revenue Per Transaction Day ("Total RPD," also referred to as "pricing") – important key metric to management and investors as it represents a measurement of the changes in underlying pricing in the vehicle rental business and encompasses the elements in vehicle rental pricing that management has the ability to control.

•Total Revenue Per Unit Per Month ("Total RPU") – important key metric to management and investors as it provides a measure of revenue productivity relative to the number of vehicles in our rental fleet whether owned or leased ("Average Rentable Vehicles"). Average Rentable Vehicles excludes vehicles for sale on our retail lots or actively in the process of being sold through other disposition channels.

•Transaction Days – important key metric to management and investors as it represents the number of revenue generating days ("volume"). It is used as a component to measure Total RPD and Vehicle Utilization. Transaction Days represent the total number of 24-hour periods, with any partial period counted as one Transaction Day, that vehicles were on rent (the period between when a rental contract is opened and closed) in a given period. Thus, it is possible for a vehicle to attain more than one Transaction Day in a 24-hour period.

Our non-GAAP measure and key metrics should not be considered in isolation and should not be considered superior to, or a substitute for, financial measures calculated in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The above non-GAAP measure and key metrics are defined, and the non-GAAP measure is reconciled to its most comparable U.S. GAAP measure, in the "Footnotes to the Results of Operations and Selected Operating Data by Segment Tables" section of this MD&A.

paragraphs: Hertz Holdings 於 2015 年在特拉華州註冊成立，作為 Rental Car Intermediate Holdings, LLC 的頂層控股公司，該公司完全擁有 Hertz，為 Hertz Global 的主要營運公司。Hertz 於 1967 年在特拉華州註冊成立，是自 1918 年以來從事車輛租賃與租賃業務的公司的繼承者。

我們主要從事車輛租賃業務，主要透過 Hertz、Dollar 和 Thrifty 品牌進行。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在全球約 160 個國家及司法管轄區運作車輛租賃業務，包括美國、歐洲、非洲、亞洲、澳洲、加拿大、加勒比地區、拉丁美洲、中東及紐西蘭，總計約 11,000 個本公司營運及特許經營據點。我們是全球最大的車輛租賃公司之一，Hertz 品牌為全球最知名的品牌之一。我們在美國及主要歐洲市場擁有廣泛的機場及非機場租賃據點網路。我們也運作 Hertz Car Sales 品牌，提供一系列品質良好、價格具有競爭力的二手車線上銷售及美國各地據點銷售。

透過我們的 "Back-to-Basics" 路線圖，我們致力於執行一項全面的戰略，以三個財務支柱為基礎：嚴謹的車隊管理、收入最佳化及嚴謹的成本控制。基於我們的品牌優勢、全球網路及車隊管理專業知識，我們持續致力於運營卓越，並將客戶視為一切工作的核心。我們透過戰略性地取得車輛、高效地部署車輛及有效地運用車輛來強化車隊。我們的作法在確保今日嚴謹執行的同時，也著重於系統性的創新，以適應不斷變化的市場動態，並為未來移動方式的可持續成長做好準備。
本公司已識別出兩個應報告分部，與其營運分部一致，如下：
•美洲 RAC - 在美國、加拿大、拉丁美洲及加勒比地區提供車輛租賃，以及車輛銷售及附加服務。我們在該分部維持廣泛的本公司營運租賃據點，並有特許經營商及合作夥伴在我們的品牌下運作租賃據點；
•國際 RAC - 在美國、加拿大、拉丁美洲及加勒比地區以外的地區提供車輛租賃，以及車輛銷售及附加服務。我們在該分部維持廣泛的本公司營運租賃據點，其中大多數位於歐洲，並有特許經營商及合作夥伴在我們的品牌下運作租賃據點。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的特許經營據點中，超過 70% 位於我們國際 RAC 分部所覆蓋的市場。
除了這兩個應報告分部，我們還有公司營運部門。我們根據營運分部的財務資訊評估表現並分配資源。
如需進一步的財務資訊，請參閱 (i) 本 2025 年年度報告第二部分第 7 項 "管理層對財務狀況與營運成果的討論及分析－營運成果與按分部選取的營運資料"，以及 (ii) 本 2025 年年度報告第二部分第 8 項 "分部資訊" 的附註 19。
HERTZ GLOBAL HOLDINGS, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES THE HERTZ CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES ITEM 1. BUSINESS (Continued)
我們的美洲RAC與國際RAC車輛租賃業務主要透過我們三大品牌—赫茲、美元與Thrifty—進行營運。我們提供多個品牌以提供客戶不同價格點、服務水準、產品與服務的完整租賃服務。這些品牌通常維持獨立的租賃據點（例如，獨立機場櫃臺），並使用不同的預訂、行銷及其他客戶接觸活動。我們透過多種方式在品牌間取得協同效益，包括利用單一車隊與車隊管理團隊，以及在適用情況下，結合車輛維護、車輛清潔與後勤作業功能。

我們的頂級品牌赫茲是全球最知名的車輛租賃品牌之一。該品牌提供優質的客戶服務，這從該品牌歷年來獲得的多項最佳車輛租賃服務獎項可見一斑，不僅在美國，也在國際上皆有表現。赫茲品牌的口號「Hertz. Let's Go!」體現我們對品質與無縫旅行的承諾。赫茲品牌透過其忠誠度計畫Hertz Gold+，以及透過我們專門車型組合所提供的車輛使用權，為客戶提供多項創新服務。赫茲品牌致力於維持其作為優質車輛租賃服務供應商的地位，透過對服務、忠誠度、品質與產品創新極度重視的策略。
我們的智慧價值品牌美元被定位為財務導向旅客的明智選擇，提供可靠且經濟的車輛租賃服務。美元品牌的重點在於透過機場車輛租賃渠道服務家庭、休閒與小型企業旅客，不僅在美國，也在國際上皆有佈局。美元品牌的口號「We never forget whose dollar it is」體現該品牌的使命，即提供可靠且價格合理的租賃體驗。
我們的深度價值品牌Thrifty以成本意識的方案競爭，為尋求優惠的旅客提供選擇。Thrifty品牌的重點在於透過機場車輛租賃渠道服務休閒旅客，不僅在美國，也在國際上皆有佈局。Thrifty品牌的口號「The Absolute Best Car for Your Money」體現該品牌著重於成為讓客戶掌握節省與花費的租賃品牌。

我們在機場與非機場據點進行品牌營運，這些據點使用共同的車隊，由共同的國家、區域與地方管理團隊監督，使用許多共同的系統，並依賴共同的車輛維護與行政中心。此外，我們的機場與非機場據點使用共同的行銷活動，並擁有許多相同的客戶。我們將這兩種據點視為單一、統一車輛租賃業務的組成部分。非機場據點在2025年與2024年的全球車輛租賃收入中佔比為34%。我們的美洲RAC車輛租賃業務在美國與加拿大設有公司自營據點。我們的國際RAC車輛租賃業務主要在澳洲、比利時、捷克共和國、法國、德國、義大利、盧森堡、荷蘭、紐西蘭、斯洛伐克、西班牙與英國設有公司自營據點。

我們在本 MD&A 中有時會使用 "we," "our," "us" 以及 "Company" 這幾個詞，用以說明與赫茲及赫茲全球相關的揭露資訊。

本 MD&A 中關於產業展望、我們對業務表現的預期以及其它非歷史性陳述，均屬展望性陳述。這些展望性陳述受到許多風險與不確定性影響，包括但不限於在項目 1A "風險因素" 中所描述的風險與不確定性。以下 MD&A 提供我們認為與理解我們合併財務狀況與營運成果相關的資訊。我們實際的結果可能與任何展望性陳述中所載或暗示的結果有重大差異。請將以下 MD&A 與標題為 "展望性陳述警示與風險因素摘要" 的部分、項目 1A "風險因素" 以及我們合併財務報表及相關附註，包含於第二部分、項目 8 的 2025 年年度報告一併閱讀。
在本 MD&A 中，我們提及以下非 GAAP 指標與關鍵指標：

•調整後企業 EBITDA – 對管理層而言重要的非 GAAP 指標，因為它允許管理層評估我們業務的營運表現，排除某些項目，並允許管理層以與營運單位利潤率衡量標準相同的方式評估整個業務表現。管理層認為，對投資者而言，這項指標同樣重要，因為它允許投資者以與管理層內部使用的相同標準評估我們的營運表現。調整後 EBITDA、營運單位利潤率衡量標準以及相應的 GAAP 指標，均為排除某些項目後計算得出，這些項目與計算調整後企業 EBITDA 所使用的項目大致相同。
•車輛使用率 – 對管理層與投資者而言重要的關鍵指標，因為它是衡量我們車輛中用來產生收入的比例，相對於可出租車隊容量。較高的車輛使用率表示有更多車輛被用來產生收入。
•每單位每月折舊費用 – 對管理階層與投資者而言為重要關鍵指標，因折舊費用與租賃費用為我們車輛租賃業務中最大的支出之一，且受車輛數量、預期處置時殘值及預期持有週期所影響。每單位每月折舊費用反映我們對車輛成本的管理方式，並有助於與車輛租賃業其他參與者進行比較。
•每交易日總收入（"總每交易日收入"，亦稱為"定價"）– 對管理階層與投資者而言為重要關鍵指標，因其代表車輛租賃業務中基礎定價變動的測量，並包含管理階層可控制的車輛租賃定價要素。
•每單位每月總收入（"總每單位收入"）– 對管理階層與投資者而言為重要關鍵指標，因其提供相對於我們租賃車隊（無論為自有或租賃）車輛數量的收入生產力測量（"平均可租車輛"）。平均可租車輛不包含零售場地待售車輛或正在透過其他處置渠道 actively 售出的車輛。
•交易日數 – 對管理階層與投資者而言為重要關鍵指標，因其代表收入產生日數（"交易量"）。其被用作測量總每交易日收入與車輛使用率的組成部分。交易日數代表在特定期間內車輛出租的總 24 小時期間數（出租合約開立與關閉之間的期間），任何部分期間均計為一個交易日。因此，一輛車在 24 小時內可能達成多個交易日數。
我們的非 GAAP 測量指標與關鍵指標不應孤立考量，也不應視為優於或取代依照美國 GAAP 計算的財務指標。上述非 GAAP 測量指標與關鍵指標在本 MD&A 的 "營運成果與分部選取營運資料表腳註" 節中已定義，並與其最相近的美國 GAAP 測量指標進行對應。

headings: 本公司車隊中程式與非程式車輛的組成，以及非程式車輛價值下降，可能使我們面臨更高的殘值風險。
我們可能無法在所期望的時間或透過所期望的管道，有效地處置非程式車輛。
若我們延長車隊的車齡，可能使車輛持有成本、客戶服務評分以及在可接受的價格和時間處置車輛的能力受到負面影響。
我們程式車輛的製造商未能履行其在回購或保證折舊計劃下的義務，可能使我們面臨那些程式車輛的損失。
製造商的安全召回可能需要對我們車隊進行昂貴且耗時的維修。
我們的車輛租賃業務特別敏感於商務與休閒旅行量的減少。
我們的業務具有高度季節性，若在旺季期間發生幹擾租賃活動的情況，可能對我們的營運成果、財務狀況、流動性及現金流造成重大不利影響。
我們可能無法準確預估未來的租賃活動水平，並根據預估調整租賃業務中車輛的數量、位置及組成。
本公司電動車隊使我們面臨多項風險。
我們可能無法充分應對影響行動產業的技術變革。
我們面臨激烈競爭，可能導致價格下滑或無法提高價格。
若客戶對網路旅遊中介平台的忠誠度高於本公司品牌，將可能對本公司業務與營業收入造成不利影響。
本公司商業離場地租賃及機場特許經營協議使我們面臨多項風險，可能導致財務結果受損。
維持良好的品牌認知度對本公司成功至關重要，若未能做到，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
吸引並留住一線員工、高階領導及其它關鍵人員的能力，對本公司業務成功至關重要。
我們可能面臨與工會代表員工相關的問題。
若我們未能評估、維護、升級及整併我們的資訊科技系統，將可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。
我們可能面臨與歐盟全球資料保護規則、加州消費者隱私權法案及其他隱私權法律法規相關的資料保護與隱私權風險。
我們的美國及海外營運業務使我們面臨可能對我們營運成果、財務狀況、流動性及現金流造成重大不利影響的風險。
營收產生車輛的處分可能導致應課稅所得，此所得可能無法完全抵銷新購營收產生車輛所產生的應課稅費用。
我們利用淨營業虧損結轉（"NOLs"）的能力，可能因根據稅法第 382 條款的股東權益變動而受到限制。
我們面臨與負債及保險相關的風險。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨重大風險與不確定性，應與本年度2025年年報中所有資訊一併謹慎考量。我們認為，本節第1A項「風險因素」所列的資訊已識別出最可能影響Hertz Global及Hertz的關鍵風險與不確定性；然而，這些並非我們在營運中所面臨的唯一風險與不確定性。目前尚未知悉或目前認為不重要的其他風險與不確定性，也可能對我們未來期間的業務、營運結果、財務狀況、流動性及現金流造成重大且不利的影響。在這種情況下，您可能損失全部或部分投資於Hertz Global普通股或The Hertz Corporation債務證券的價值。您應謹慎考量下列每一項風險與不確定性。任何下列風險與不確定性都可能對我們未來期間的業務、營運結果、財務狀況、流動性及現金流造成重大且不利的影響。

我們在車隊中使用程式車與非程式車。對於程式車，車輛製造商同意以指定價格購回車輛，或在指定時間內保證車輛的折舊率。在車隊中使用程式車可降低我們的殘值風險，並為這些車輛提供固定的折舊。此外，程式車提供靈活性，因為我們可能在某些時間段內以較高價值出售某些程式車，這使我們能更有效地管理車輛供應，以應對租賃需求高峯時期。這些好處會隨著車隊中程式車數量減少而降低，這在近年來通常為常態，但情況正在改善。我們無法保證我們能取得合適比例的程式車與非程式車。
我們車隊中絕大多數車輛為非程式車。整體而言，我們持有的非程式車比例使我們面臨殘值風險。非程式車的殘值下降，或殘值未能遵循歷史模式，可能會導致出售這些車輛時產生重大損失，或在我們擁有這些車輛期間加速折舊。這些結果都可能對我們的營運結果、財務狀況、流動性及現金流造成重大且不利的影響。
車輛殘值會因市場條件及季節性波動而有所變動。若車輛殘值下降，我們可能面臨更高的車輛銷售損失風險、折舊費用增加、對營運結果產生負面影響，也可能面臨在車隊融資設施中滿足擔保要求的困難。
若我們車隊中非程式車的殘值下降，且這些殘值未能改善，可能會導致我們持有車輛時間更長，出售這些車輛時產生重大損失，或在擁有這些車輛期間需以比預期更快速的折舊率進行折舊。
若車隊中車輛的市場價值下降，或我們在二手車市場銷售車輛的能力嚴重受限，我們可能難以符合資產擔保融資安排中的擔保要求，這將迫使我們減少債務本金或提供更多擔保（以現金、車輛及/或某些其他契約權利形式）給相關債權人。
